newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross HIV compensation reaches 13.7 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross HIV compensation reaches 13.7 bln yen.

text.p: Green Cross Corp said on Tuesday that compensation payments to patients who were infected with the HIV virus through its blood products totalled 13.7 billion yen as of the end of May.
The company said in a statement that it settled on May 27 a legal liability suit filed by 118 plaintiffs by agreeing to pay compensation totalling about 1.5 billion yen.
The company said most of the compensation payments arising from the latest legal settlement have already been earmarked as extraordinary losses in 1995/96 and 1996/97.
The Osaka-based pharmaceuticals company has been at the centre of a scandal concerning HIV-tainted blood products.
Former Green Cross executives were indicted last October on charges of professional negligence for selling blood products that could infect patients with HIV.
The company has estimated that it faces compensation payments totalling 24 billion yen to haemophiliacs who were infected by its blood products.

The company is scheduled to merge into another Osaka-based drug company, Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, on April 1, 1998. The date of the merger was postponed last month from the original target of October 1.
